title: Separate slow dependency transport from native test execution
applies_when: An authorized native test worker cannot finish downloading public dependencies, or a task-private Python environment is intended to reuse inherited base packages. Another authorized machine may retrieve exact artifacts, or a concrete hypothesis may be testable without missing test-only dependencies. Preserve failed setup separately from tests that actually ran.
lesson: Keep versions and artifact identity fixed; change delivery, not the test contract. Download target-compatible wheels, verify provenance and hashes, transfer them to a task-private wheelhouse, and install with the target interpreter using --no-index and --find-links. Select the target Python version, ABI, platform and architecture explicitly when the download machine differs. A pip --target directory is not automatically a site directory: adding it to sys.path does not process its .pth files. Review the wheel's path configuration; use a normal private environment, reviewed site.addsitedir, or an explicit equivalent package path. Check the imported dependency's __file__ before testing, not only distribution metadata: new metadata can coexist with an old globally imported module. Artifact reuse and installer-cache acceptance are separate: uv distinguishes registry, URL and local sources, so exact local wheels need not satisfy the original offline project sync. With uv's --system-site-packages, Python can access inherited base distributions, but uv list/install ignore them. Inspect the actual child prefix and import paths before assuming zero-download or offline reuse; where upstream requires uv, prepare its explicit private closure. If using uv run --no-sync after independently materializing locked artifacts, verify actual installed versions, dependency consistency, imported source and native ABI, then run real tests; report that route rather than claiming the original sync succeeded. For Go, a file-based module proxy can deliver the same versions while the native go command verifies the existing go.sum values. If only a release Git source is accessible, a separately reviewed private go.work can map exact target/dependency exports as local main modules. Bind commits, raw-file manifests and resolved module directories; leave upstream go.mod/go.sum unchanged and disable module downloads. This needs a workspace-capable compiler and qualifies an explicit workspace, not module-ZIP hashes or original single-module resolution. If only upstream test dependencies are blocked and the production package itself builds offline, a separate stdlib-only public-caller test package can answer a specific hypothesis against the complete original source and module files. Label this supplementary probe separately; do not rename it an upstream baseline. Account separately for acquisition, transfer, install and tests; a fast cached install is not end-to-end setup cost or a measured method advantage.
avoid_when: Do not route around permission, policy or authentication denials. Do not substitute older dependencies, replace required integration tests with a small probe, disable known hash checks or treat an absent wheel as successful qualification. Do not narrow the project's supported Python/platform range just to make offline universal resolution pass, or hand-edit opaque installer caches to fabricate hits. A public-caller reproduction establishes observed behavior, not accepted semantics, novelty or PR readiness; check existing author work before implementing a competing fix. Do not remove production files or mock missing runtime dependencies to make the probe build. Matching version strings do not prove equal bytes or native ABI compatibility; --no-sync does not check that an environment is current. Missing target wheels or build prerequisites need an explicit different approach. Local-only package resolution is not network/process isolation, and a private venv is not an untrusted-code sandbox. This is documented delivery guidance, not a general speedup, native test result or PR-yield claim.

evidence.note: Official documentation distinguishes runtime access to inherited packages from uv list/install behavior. Import success is not evidence of installer reuse, offline resolution or measured setup savings. Recheck the target installer/version; do not write into a shared base or change required project tooling to evade a denial.
pip documents downloading distributions separately and installing locally using --no-index/--find-links. This supports the delivery mechanism, not any unpublished timing or target-project result.

site.addsitedir adds a directory and processes its .pth files; import lines in those files execute code. Plain sys.path insertion is not this operation. Review trusted artifacts before processing them. These documented mechanisms do not qualify an installed dependency, compiler or GPU kernel.

--target installs packages into a specified directory. It does not establish which module a separate interpreter imports, install every omitted dependency under --no-deps, or prove native ABI compatibility.
The download command supports explicit target platform, Python version, implementation and ABI. A wheel collected on one host is not automatically appropriate for another.

uv documents source-dependent cache identities and warns against direct cache modification. Matching artifact hashes and versions do not by themselves establish an original project sync's cache acceptance.

uv run normally locks and syncs automatically; --no-sync skips checking whether the environment is up to date. Independent environment verification and native tests remain necessary, and are not results supplied by this documentation.
The module reference documents file-based proxy delivery and native verification against known go.sum hashes. Transport success does not replace module authentication or package tests.
An explicit GOWORK selects local main modules. This changes resolution; independently verify exact source identities and do not claim the original module download/sum checks passed.

Package-list mode tests the explicitly selected packages; imported production packages are built without automatically running their own tests. A separate public-caller package can therefore answer a focused question without establishing full upstream-suite qualification.

An existing author already fixes the non-string-key panic in the ToStringMapInt/Int64 reflection path. A reproduced behavior is not necessarily an unclaimed contribution. The author's reported full-suite result is not independent qualification by this knowledge card.
